newsitem.title: UK: Guinness shares slip on currency woes.
newsitem.headline: Guinness shares slip on currency woes.

text.p: Shares in drinks group Guinness were off 5p at 430p by 1245 GMT as analysts talked in disappointed terms about the size of the group's anticipated hit from continued sterling strength on foreign exchange markets.
"The actual underlying trading is exactly as expected, in other words small improvements, but the currency hit is more than most people were anticipating," said Merrill Lynch analyst John Beaumont.
In a trading update issued earlier the company said it expected its trading profit to suffer by some six percent or 60 million pounds in 1997 as a result of sterling's strength.
Grand Metropolitan Plc fell 7-1/2p to 425p. At a rate of $1.60 to the pound, GrandMet stands to lose about 16 million in profit every year.

"It's really quite a negative statement," said one analyst who chose not to be named. "The only thing that seems to be growing is brewing. We are not too worried now about 1996 but the 60 million hit in 1997 means we will have to bring our forecasts down by about 40 million odd."
The company's currency loss will be in part offset by a saving on lower interest payment on its debt which analysts estimate means a benefit of 10-15 million.
Guinness said its interest coupon would be over one percentage point lower in 1997 compared with 1996.
According to a Reuter survey of 25 brokers taken on January 10, the consensus forecast for Guinness' pretax profits in the year ended December 31, 1997 was 1.017 billion.
But most analysts now do not expect the company to breach the 1.0 billion mark. For 1996, the same brokers forecast on average pretax profits of 958.5 million and an EPS of 33.9p.
